Mode-B finding: SBC-doubled-YoY while cash returns are token is mild capital-allocation under-emphasis.

summary: CLB's FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-02-15) reads as a clean, modestly profitable international oil-services name that does not match the distressed profile implied by its -33.6% drawdown. The forensic file is unusually quiet: KPMG (Big-4, 9-year tenure) issued an unqualified ICFR opinion with no critical audit matter beyond the procedural redomestication-tax question; no going-concern language; covenant ratios (1.76x leverage, 6.37x interest coverage) sit comfortably inside their 2.50x/3.00x respective floors with no amendment history; Q1'24 10-Q reaffirms the same ratios; staggered Senior Notes maturity ladder (2026/2028/2028/2030) with no wall; revolver $69.1M undrawn; and twenty-four Form 4 filings pre-cutoff contain zero open-market insider sales (only RSU vesting, tax withholding, and grants — including a 234,124-share director grant accepted in February 2024). The honest-disclosure findings are mild: ~70% of the headline +88% YoY net-income growth comes from a one-time $11.6M deferred-tax-liability reversal tied to the May 2023 Luxembourg-to-Delaware redomestication (adjusted growth ~30%); stock-based comp doubled YoY to $14.0M against $4.1M of cash returns; and $15.1M of cash is substantially all held by foreign subsidiaries, including a Russian subsidiary whose earnings are explicitly not expected to be repatriated. These are MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY items, not distress signals. The framework's exclusion-of-liars discipline finds nothing to exclude here.
